issues.description: The spec theme is 'a surprise birthday party', but nothing in the dialogue is a surprise: Ben already knows about his party and Anna openly confirms the cake. The theme is only half delivered (birthday party, yes; surprise, no).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the surprise element explicit with A2-level wording, e.g. change s1l2 to 'Great! Is it a surprise for my birthday party?' and s1l3 to 'Yes! A big cake - don't look!'}, or reframe the party as a surprise for someone else ('Is it for Mum's surprise birthday party?').

issues.description: Interaction prompt 'What were you doing when a friend called you last time?' is understandable but not how a native speaker would phrase it; 'last time' dangles awkwardly at the end of the when-clause.
issues.suggested_fix: Rephrase as 'What were you doing the last time a friend called you?'

qa_report.summary: A clean A2 micro-dialogue. Line 1 models past continuous with 'when' accurately and the grammar note explains it correctly with a matching example. All vocabulary is at or below A2; target word 'birthday' and review words 'party' and 'cake' all appear naturally, and the three glosses are accurate and simpler than the words they explain. Two minor points: the 'surprise' element of the theme is not realised in the dialogue, and the interaction prompt is slightly unidiomatic ('when a friend called you last time' -> 'the last time a friend called you'). Neither blocks approval.
